key_insight: ConforNets introduces a latent-variable control module inside OpenFold3 that lets the model generate and switch between biologically relevant protein conformations reliably, rather than predicting a single dominant state.
problem_solved: AlphaFold-family models often return one predominant structure and struggle to recover alternative, functionally important conformations; prior fixes used ad-hoc inference perturbations that are inefficient and inconsistent.
method: Integrate a learned latent conditioning pathway into OpenFold3 that modulates internal representations to steer conformation.
Train a latent encoder/decoder (or conditional prior) to map between latent codes and distinct conformational modes, enabling targeted sampling of alternate states.
Perform controlled latent sampling and refinement to reproducibly recover major conformational clusters far more efficiently than inference-time perturbations.
impact: Provides a systematic, trainable mechanism to explore protein conformational landscapes within a high-performance folding model, improving sampling efficiency and enabling downstream tasks (e.g., drug binding, enzyme engineering) that require alternate states.
visual_elements: Architecture schematic: OpenFold3 block diagram with an injected 'latent control' module and arrows showing conditioning flow.
Side-by-side 3D render: dominant AF-predicted structure vs. alternate ConforNets-generated conformation for the same sequence.
Latent space map (UMAP/t-SNE): clusters colored by recovered conformational modes with example structures.
Bar/line chart: qualitative comparison of sampling efficiency and mode-recovery consistency (ConforNets vs. inference perturbations).
paper_title: ConforNets: Latents-Based Conformational Control in OpenFold3
paper_authors: Minji Lee, Colin Kalicki, Minkyu Jeon, Aymen Qabel, Alisia Fadini
